description: Used to politely request something or place an order.
Used to ask what something is when you don't know its name or identity.
Used to ask whether something exists or is available.
Used to ask for directions to a place.

examples.en: How do I get to Hongdae?
How do I get to Myeongdong?
How do I get to the airport?

description: Used to say that you want to go to a place.

examples.en: I want to go to Jeju Island.
I want to go to Hongdae!
I want to go to the Han River.

description: Ask for someone's opinion about something. Say what you need, then add 어때요 at th
Decide on one option when ordering or choosing. Just place a noun before 로 할게요 —

examples.en: I'll go with the large size.

description: Ask if someone has ever experienced something before. It works in casual and pol

examples.en: Have you ever been to a noraebang?
Have you ever worn a hanbok?

description: Ask someone to give you a recommendation. Just place a noun before 추천해 주세요 — no
Politely request someone to do something for you. Say what you need, then add 주실

examples.en: Could you take a photo for me?
Could you explain a bit more?
examples.ko: 조금 더 설명해 주실 수 있어요?

description: Say what you like or enjoy. Say what you need, then add 좋아해요 at the end. Common
Express that something is surprisingly fascinating or unique. Say what you need,

examples.en: I've never seen this food before — it's fascinating.
It's fascinating how thorough the recycling is.

description: Ask for more of something you already have. Just place a noun before 더 주세요 — no

examples.en: Please give me more side dishes.

description: Politely ask for a lower price on something. Just place a noun before 깎아 주세요 — n

examples.en: Please give me a small discount!
Please give me a discount if I buy two.

description: Ask if someone has ever tried using something. Say what you need, then add 써봤어요
Ask which option someone prefers. It works in casual and polite speech alike. Co
Say something is more or less than you expected. It works in casual and polite s

examples.en: It's not as hard as I thought.

english: I'm so happy we're all together
description: Express happiness that everyone is gathered together. It works in casual and pol

examples.en: I'm so happy we're all together!
I'm happy to be together with my whole family.
It's great to be together with all my friends!

description: Say that something has already been done. It works in casual and polite speech a
Say you feel nervous or excited about something important. Just place a noun bef

examples.en: I'm nervous because it's my first presentation.
I'm so nervous — will it be okay?
My heart is pounding — I'm so nervous!

description: Say which country or city you come from. Just place a noun before 에서 왔어요 — no co
Use when meeting someone to ask for their cooperation. Say what you need, then a

examples.en: I look forward to working with you.
Please take care of me today!

description: Ask where to board a specific type of transport. Just place a noun before 어디서 타요

examples.en: Where do I get on Line 2?
Where do I get on the bus?
Where do I get on the airport bus?

description: Say what food you want to eat right now. Just place a noun before 먹고 싶어요 — no co
Say what you cannot eat due to allergy or preference. Say what you need, then ad
Ask permission before eating something. Just place a noun before 먹어도 돼요 — no con

examples.en: Is it okay to eat here?
Is it okay to eat this?
Is it okay to eat now?

description: Ask permission to call someone by a certain name. Just place a noun before 불러도 돼

examples.en: Is it okay to call you 언니?
Is it okay to call you 오빠?
Is it okay to call you by your name?

description: Say you'd like to come back to a place again. Just place a noun before 또 오고 싶어요

examples.en: I want to come here again!
I want to come back to Korea.
I want to come back to this café!

description: Say which mode of transport you are taking. Just place a noun before 타요 — no con
Say where you get off a bus or subway. Say what you need, then add 에서 내려요 at the

examples.en: Get off at Hongik University Station.
Get off at the next stop.

description: Tell a driver where you want to be taken. Just place a noun before 까지 가 주세요 — no

examples.en: Please take me to the airport.

description: Ask for food to be prepared with less of a certain quality. It works in casual a
Ask if a food or drink can be refilled for free. Just place a noun before 리필 돼요

examples.en: Can I get a refill of kimchi?
Can I get a refill of side dishes?
Can I get a refill of water?

description: Ask what someone is doing at a time or place. Just place a noun before 에 뭐 해요 —

examples.en: What are you doing this weekend?

description: Invite someone to do something together with you. It works in casual and polite

examples.en: Do you want to eat together?
Do you want to watch a movie together?
Do you want to take a walk together?

description: Tell someone you are going to be a little late. It works in casual and polite sp

examples.en: I think I'll be a little late.
I think I'll be 10 minutes late.
I think I'll be quite late — sorry.

description: Tell someone you are lost and need directions. It works in casual and polite spe

examples.en: I'm lost — can I look at your map?
examples.ko: 길을 잃었어요, 지도 좀 봐도 돼요?

description: Tell someone to simply go straight ahead. Say what you need, then add 쭉 가면 돼요 at

examples.en: Just go straight down this road.
If you go straight, there's a café.

description: Tell someone which direction to turn. Just place a noun before 으로 꺾으면 돼요 — no co

examples.en: Turn left at the traffic light.
Turn right at the convenience store.

description: Ask if someone has seen or watched something. Say what you need, then add 봤어요 at

examples.en: Have you been to Jeju Island?
Have you watched a Korean drama?

description: Say that something is fun or interesting. Say what you need, then add 재미있어요 at t
Strongly recommend something you found great. Say what you need, then add 강추예요 a
Ask about the weather in a place or at a time. Just place a noun before 날씨 어때요 —

examples.en: What's the weather like in Seoul?

description: Say it looks like rain, snow, or something is coming. Just place a noun before 올

examples.en: It looks like it's going to snow.
It looks like it's going to rain.
It looks like I'm going to be late.

description: Compare two things, saying one is more or less than the other. Say what you need

examples.en: This one is tastier than that one.
